acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Required PTO dates, contributing holidays and remaining balances reconcile; zero PTO remains feasible and insufficient balances are rejected.

Source inspection confirms weekends do not shift holidays and each holiday date grants at most one exemption. Repository fixtures additionally cover zero balance, exact limits and cross-year accounting, but their execution was blocked.

tests.command: node -e <independent in-memory TypeScript transpilation and exhaustive date-window oracle>
tests.evidence: Loaded actual calendar.ts/index.ts through typescript.transpileModule and Module._compile without writes. For each timezone America/New_York and Pacific/Auckland, compared all durations 1–30 over 12 monthly starts in leap year 2028, with search ranges capped at 41 days, balance 6 and duplicate holidays on the first date. Independent noon-UTC enumeration compared top-three ranked starts and exact PTO dates, then checked remaining balances. 360 comparisons passed per timezone; elapsed 226ms and 212ms respectively. This does not substitute for repository fixtures or annual worst-case performance checks.
Initial heredoc invocation failed before Node execution because zsh could not create its temporary heredoc file. Repeated successfully using node -e without temporary files.

findings.evidence: Approved Domain contracts require VacationOpportunity assumptions and deterministic rank reason, and CalculationResult validated opportunities or explicit no-results with structured validation errors. VacationOpportunity contains neither assumptions nor rank reason; optimizePto at line 104 returns only an array and throws ZodError for invalid inputs. Ranking/assumption copy and no-results guidance instead live in PtoPlanner. A direct domain consumer receives [] without an explicit result discriminator and must reconstruct explanation policy. Align the public domain contract with approved requirements or obtain an explicit requirement adjustment.
